primary_sources.finding: IP configuration exposes sslMode and deprecated requireSsl. The engine-specific compatibility table and mode priority govern interpretation; the trusted-client mode excludes SQL Server.
Native REST schema corroborates the encryption and legacy fields used by the collector.
SQL Server exposes allow-both and encrypted-only modes. Client driver encryption defaults do not prove server enforcement; proxy encryption is separate.
Encrypted-only suffices for encryption enforcement without requiring mutual TLS; proxy-only application connectivity is not established by these instance fields.

findings.detail: Current perimeter callback synthesizes unspecified mode and requireSsl=false from an empty config and emits FAIL. No collected value proves enforcement is disabled; return UNKNOWN.

Both current callbacks accept trusted-client mode for SQL Server, although it is outside native engine applicability. This invalid native response must remain UNKNOWN; it does not prove runtime plaintext.

MySQL/PostgreSQL encrypted-only with requireSsl=true is outside documented compatible pairs. sslMode has priority, but compatibility validation is still required for a valid native declaration; helper conservatively reports UNKNOWN, never infers runtime FAIL.
Pinned Steampipe policy permits only encrypted-only and therefore alarms on valid PostgreSQL/MySQL trusted-client mode. Existing native implementation already repairs this; retain it.

Explicit-mode callback cannot classify an observed legacy true field when sslMode is absent. The same native encryption requirement is proven by the legacy boolean; shared helper supports fallback without requiring client certificates.

minimal_root_integration.change: Add databaseVersion=POSTGRES_16 to trusted-client PASS example; change perimeter FAIL example requireSsl from true to false so it is a valid native allow-both combination; include legacy fallback and missing-value UNKNOWN cases. Describe encryption with sslMode or an explicit legacy boolean, engine applicability, and unresolved invalid combinations.

helper_contract.policy: Encryption enforcement only; never strengthens to mutual TLS. Explicit native allow-both FAIL; encrypted-only PASS; trusted-client PASS only for known MySQL/PostgreSQL; fallback only absent/unspecified mode plus explicit bool; missing/malformed/unreadable/future/unsupported/conflicting values UNKNOWN. Generic explicit modes need no invented engine if no legacy compatibility ambiguity exists.
helper_contract.source_priority: A recognized sslMode drives the status for valid pairs. requireSsl=false must not veto MySQL/PostgreSQL encrypted-only; conflict handling records UNKNOWN rather than assuming which stale/invalid native observation is reliable.

adjacent_controls: Public IP, private IP, authorized network and user-connection-count/logging checks have distinct predicates; no TLS change is proposed for them. Their collector fields are preserved by the same native projection.
